gloss: to have someone look at; please take a look (humble)

definitions.gloss: to have someone (superior) look at; to show to a respected person
definitions.explanation: A humble expression used when asking or describing the action of a respected person viewing, reading, or watching something. Combines the honorific ご{覧|らん} (looking) with the humble auxiliary いただく (to receive the favor of).

examples.japanese: ぜひご{覧|らん}いただきたいです。
examples.english: I would very much like you to see it.

examples.japanese: {資料|しりょう}をご{覧|らん}いただけますか。
examples.english: Could you please take a look at the materials?

examples.japanese: {本日|ほんじつ}はお{忙|いそが}しい{中|なか}、{展示|てんじ}をご{覧|らん}いただきありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you for taking the time to view the exhibition today despite your busy schedule.

notes:
A polite/humble expression combining ご{覧|らん} (honorific form of {見|み}る, to see) with いただく (humble auxiliary meaning "to receive the favor of"). Used in business, customer service, and formal settings.

POLITENESS LEVELS FOR "TO SEE/LOOK":
- {見|み}る: plain (neutral)
- ご{覧|らん}になる: honorific ({尊敬語|そんけいご}) — the other person sees
- ご{覧|らん}いただく: humble ({謙譲語|けんじょうご}) — I receive the favor of them seeing
- {拝見|はいけん}する: humble — I humbly look at something

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ご{覧|らん}いただけますか: could you please look at this?
- ご{覧|らん}いただきたい: I would like you to see this
- ご{覧|らん}いただきありがとうございます: thank you for viewing
- ご{覧|らん}いただければ{幸|さいわ}いです: I would be grateful if you could look at this

USAGE:
This expression is used when the speaker wants a superior or customer to view something. It is NOT used to describe one's own viewing — for that, use {拝見|はいけん}する.
